blogs.title: Procedural Rights in Vacuo: The D.C. Circuit Reinforces the 'Concrete Interest' Requirement for Standing
blogs.description: This post analyzes the court's rigorous application of *Summers v. Earth Island Institute* to reject the plaintiff's claim of a standalone procedural right. It examines Judge Katsas's distinction between a statutory mandate to investigate and a citizen's enforceable right to the outcome of that investigation, arguing that the ruling tightens the screws on 'informational standing' by requiring plaintiffs to prove a direct link between the procedural violation and a concrete, particularized harm beyond mere curiosity.

blogs.title: The Attenuated Chain: Why Speculation About Agency Enforcement Breaks Causation
blogs.description: Focusing on the causation prong of Article III standing, this article dissects the court's rejection of AFL's argument that an OSC investigation would inevitably lead to record production. It explores how the D.C. Circuit utilized recent Supreme Court precedent (*FDA v. Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine*) to declare that relying on the discretionary choices of non-parties (the MSPB and DOJ) renders any claimed injury too speculative to sustain jurisdiction, effectively insulating OSC's enforcement discretion from judicial review via third-party suits.

blogs.title: Statutory Interpretation vs. Jurisdictional Gatekeeping: The OSC Investigation Mandate Remains Unresolved
blogs.description: While the district court held that Section 1216 mandates an OSC investigation regardless of FOIA predicates, this blog post argues that the appellate dismissal leaves that critical statutory question unanswered due to the threshold standing hurdle. The analysis discusses the tension between Congress's apparent intent in 5 U.S.C. § 1216(a)(3) and the judiciary's reluctance to intervene in administrative enforcement schemes when no aggrieved party can demonstrate a redressable injury, potentially leaving a gap in FOIA oversight.
